title: A money approval may resolve without a click, and one payment request can leave two live approval cards
root_cause: Suspected, not reproduced. A payment raised by a peer run (Chief messages the Mercury agent) is paused in packages/adapters/src/executor.ts near 3990-4010 (pauseRunForInput, then notifyRun). On run resume the approval is re-issued instead of reusing the pending card, which produced a second live card for one $300 request; and in one walk a $1,200 card read Approved with no click, after Chief relayed the user's 'Yes, pay ...' text. If relayed text counts as approval, that is a money-safety bug. P0 stays only until a clean single-user repro either confirms or clears it; if it clears, J2-03 alone keeps the cluster at P1.
verification: Suspected. Not seen by any other walker (R1 and J3 approved a $1,200 card by clicking and saw normal behaviour). Code read: the pause path exists at executor.ts:3990-4010; the re-issue and relay handling were not traced. packages/adapters/src/executor-approval-replay.test.ts already exists and is the place for a failing test.
files: packages/adapters/src/executor.ts (approval pause and resume near 3990-4010; reuse the pending card on resume, mark superseded cards unusable, a denial of a stale card must not rewrite an approved outcome)
packages/adapters/src/executor-approval-replay.test.ts (failing regression first: relayed 'Yes, pay' text does not resolve a money card; resume does not create a second live card)
apps/api approval resolution path (only an authenticated click or approve call resolves a money card; locate with grep for the ask-resolve route)
reach: Anyone who lets an agent pay a bill. Wrong result is a duplicate or unapproved payment.
acceptance_criteria: Failing test first: a Chief-relayed user message never resolves a payment approval card; only the card's Send does.
One payment request produces exactly one live card across a page reload and a run resume; an older card reads 'No longer active' and cannot be pressed.
Denying a superseded card does not change the recorded outcome of the approved one, and the agent's final message matches the real outcome.
Repro walk with one user on a clean thread: ask Chief to pay $300 to a known recipient, navigate away mid-run, return: one card, one decision, one result message.

title: The approval toast opens or clears the wrong chat, vanishes after a reload, and the next card slides under the pointer
root_cause: apps/web/src/lib/approval-toasts.ts keys each toast by toast.href (one chat id, line 70-72). notifyRun in packages/adapters/src/executor.ts:4004 passes the peer run's thread, so a Mercury approval raised for Chief links to Chief, where no card exists; opening the Mercury chat never matches that key, so the toast stays. The same string compare misses per-email chats (email agent panel). The map lives in memory, so a reload shows no toast for a live card. After an approval is answered the next card renders in the same screen position with live buttons.
verification: J2-02 and J3-03 observed. Code confirmed: approval-toasts.ts:70 keys by toast.href and dismissApprovalToasts(chat) compares that string only; executor.ts:4004 passes threadId of the run that holds the pause. R1 saw the toast still present 3 s after answering (partly met). J2-11 and J2-10 observed once each, cause read from code only (in-memory pending map).
files: packages/adapters/src/executor.ts (notifyRun near 4004: pass the bot and thread that hold the card)
apps/web/src/lib/approval-toasts.ts (match the open chat by bot and thread, including per-email chats; rebuild pending toasts from unanswered approvals on load)
apps/web/src/components/AppToaster.tsx
approval card component (disable Send and Deny for about 1 s after a new card replaces one in place)
apps/web/src/lib/approval-toasts.test.ts
reach: Everyone who approves anything from a bot other than the one they are talking to; most money approvals.
acceptance_criteria: A toast raised for a peer run opens the chat that holds the card in one tap.
Opening that chat, or answering the card in a second tab, removes the toast within 2 s.
Opening an email agent chat removes the toast for that email's card.
Reload with a pending approval shows one toast again.
A card that appears where a decided card was has disabled buttons for 1 s.
conflicts_with: C8 (same approval-toasts.ts and AppToaster.tsx; do C2 first, then C8)
reopens: iteration 9 C1 (removal within 2 s was only partly met)

title: Settings says AI is allowed while Inbox, Legal and agents say it is not, and the agents link to Integrations for the fix
root_cause: The Allow AI models switch counts only recipients with use === 'model' (apps/web/src/components/AiDataSharing.tsx:119) and reads on when those are allowed. Inbox asks for the recipient in triageBlocked (Inbox.tsx:951-955) and Legal and agents check their own recipient, so a recipient outside that filter is blocked yet invisible in Settings. Separately the agent hand-off text at packages/adapters/src/executor.ts:8358-8370 ends every failure with [Open Integrations], which cannot fix a missing AI consent.
verification: Observed on screen by FLOW (switch on, Inbox card, Legal banner, Investors agent all 'not allowed') and by J2 (Investors agent 'Open Integrations' while Gmail shows Connected). Code confirmed for the filter at AiDataSharing.tsx:119 and the generic link at executor.ts:8358 and :8370. The recipient mismatch is suspected; it may come from demo seed data, but the on-screen contradiction is real.
files: apps/web/src/components/AiDataSharing.tsx (derive the switch from the same recipient list Inbox, Legal and agents check)
apps/web/src/pages/Inbox.tsx:949-955 and apps/web/src/pages/Legal.tsx (read the same state)
packages/adapters/src/executor.ts:8358-8370 (consent failures link to Settings > Privacy and approvals; unknown-recipient failures get no Integrations link)
apps/web/src/components/AiDataSharing.test.tsx
reach: Every new user who connects mail or documents; consent is the gate to Inbox sorting, Legal, Data room and agent answers.
acceptance_criteria: With the switch on, no consent card appears on Inbox, Legal or Data room, and no agent answers 'not permitted'.
If any area is blocked the switch reads off and the blocked message links to that switch.
No agent reply for a consent or unknown-recipient failure ends in 'Open Integrations'.
Unit test: a recipient with any use that blocks Inbox also turns the switch off.
conflicts_with: C6 (Legal consent and banner use the same state; do C3 first)

title: First Inbox sort shows only grey bars for minutes, and a revisit shows 'First sync' on a synced mailbox
root_cause: While the first sort runs, Inbox.tsx:664 hides every row (sortingRows) and the page waits for two full poll cycles (TRIAGE_MAX_POLLS then one auto-retry, lines 475-486) before it shows the stall notice. 'sorting' only clears when a pending-to-done change is seen (:551-553), so a mailbox where the last poll lands after the change stays in skeletons until a reload. The same loading branch drops the previous rows on a space switch and prints 'First sync can take a minute' for a synced account.
verification: Observed by J1 (14 mails, over 105 s, reload showed the sorted list at once) and V2 (over 3 min, several reloads). A 1-mail mailbox sorted in 9 s. Code confirmed at Inbox.tsx:475-486, :551-553, :664. FLOW-04 observed once on a loaded shared stack; load may be a cause, so it ships with this cluster as the lower-confidence part.
files: apps/web/src/pages/Inbox.tsx (after about 15 s of sorting, show the unsorted rows with a 'Sorting...' line; clear sorting when polling stops and re-read the list once; keep cached rows on a space revisit; show 'First sync' only for an account that has never synced)
apps/web/src/pages/Inbox.test.tsx
reach: Every user's first morning (STORY-INB-022) and every large mailbox.
acceptance_criteria: On a 14-mail mailbox rows are readable within 15 s of pressing Allow, or a Retry notice shows by then.
After the last poll the list is re-read once; no skeleton remains once triage is done.
Switching space and back shows the last rows at once with no 'First sync' sentence.
Test: sorting stuck at triagePending=true past the limit shows rows, not skeletons.
decision_question: The first sort hides all rows on purpose, so the To do card does not push them down (Inbox.tsx:663). Is showing unsorted rows after 15 s acceptable, or should the page keep hiding them? Recommend showing them dimmed.
reopens: iteration 9 C4 (stalled-sort retry could not be tested then)

title: The Connect Gmail dialog resets to its first question after Connect, and Inbox 'Connect mail' takes five steps

title: Legal 'Scan now' replaced reviewed contract values and removed deadlines without a message
root_cause: Suspected. LEGAL_SCAN_PROMPT (apps/api/src/legal-agent.ts:21) tells the agent to re-record every document, and the legal_upsert tools overwrite fields with whatever the model extracts. With placeholder PDFs the model returned less, so Term dates went empty, Office Lease value $90,000 became $9,000, and 13 deadlines became 4 (non-renewal notices and auto-renewal rows vanished). Only hand-added deadlines survived.
verification: Observed by J2 once with before and after screenshots. Cause is a hypothesis; the demo uses blank placeholder PDFs, so it may be a demo artifact. Code read: legal-agent.ts:21 prompt. The upsert tools were not traced.
files: apps/api/src/legal-agent.ts (prompt: update only changed documents)
legal_upsert tool implementations in apps/api or packages/adapters (never replace a field a person has seen with an empty or lower-confidence value; never delete open derived deadlines on re-scan)
Legal page (show 'N changed' with Undo after a scan)
regression test for upsert merge
reach: Anyone who presses Scan now on Legal after reviewing contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Failing test first: re-scanning a document whose extraction returns empty term and value keeps the stored values.
A re-scan never deletes an open deadline derived from a document that still exists.
After a scan the page states how many rows changed and offers Undo.
decision_question: Should a re-scan ever overwrite a field the founder has edited or reviewed? Recommend no: edited fields are locked and the scan only fills blanks.
